content.title: About
content.content: Chili with meat is a spicy dish made from ground meat (beef, pork or a blend), tomatoes, beans, spices and chili peppers. It is popular in Mexican and American cuisines and is often served with rice, tortillas or bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally chili is cooked in earthenware pots, allowing flavors to develop slowly.
There are more than 150 varieties of chili peppers, each giving a different level of heat.
The United States hosts the annual World Chili Championship where chefs from many states compete.
In Texas, “chili con carne” is often prepared without beans, while most other regions include them.
Chili with meat is a common comfort food after sporting events.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and pork contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomatoes and spices
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and capsaicin from chili have anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Fiber from beans
items.content: Beans add dietary fiber, promoting digestive health.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot versions can irritate the stomach and esophagus in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared spice mixes often contain a lot of salt; monitor the amount used.

items.title: Allergy to meat or beans
items.content: Some people may be allergic to beef, pork or legumes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑rich due to meat and oil; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve hot chili with meat alongside rice, mashed potatoes, tortillas, croutons or grated cheese. Garnish with sour cream, avocado or fresh herbs as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the chili to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
